title: The Atacama Desert
text: The Atacama Desert is a plateau in South America covering a 1,600 km strip of land on the Pacific coast of the continent, west of the Andes, primarily in Chile. It is considered the driest non-polar desert in the world, with some weather stations never having recorded rain. The average precipitation in the Atacama is just 1 mm per year. Paradoxically, the desert experiences dense fog (called camanchaca) that rolls in from the Pacific, sustaining some plant and animal life. The Atacama is rich in copper and other minerals and contains the world's largest lithium reserves. Its clear, dry skies make it one of the best locations on Earth for astronomical observatories.
